doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The long Metropole bandstand, dashing to Birdland and sitting in with Duke
summary: She loved hearing Woody Herman's band strung across the Metropole's narrow stage, then going to Birdland to hear Phineas Newborn, Bud and Duke, who always invited her to sit in.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: . . . across the length of the bandstand. The Woody Herman band would play in there. It would be ridiculous, because at one end would be the drums and piano, and at the far end would be the brass section. I don’t know how they ever got together. They’d all look in the mirror. There was a mirror on the opposite side of the club. Somehow they managed to play together. I just loved to go in there all the time to hear them or Red Allen or whoever was there when we were through at the Hickory House. I’m so lucky. I had such wonderful musical experiences of every kind of music, because then we’d dash over to Birdland and we’d hear . . . Phineas Newborn was in town by that time, I think. Your buddy, Phineas. We’d hear him a lot and Bud and Duke. Duke would always invite me to sit in with the band. Whenever he saw me in a club he would . . .
You actually sat in with the band?

They would all . . . They would play the blues or something. I knew their repertoire anyway. It was always something . . . there was no hard piano part to read. I would just fit in and have a ball. He always did that for me.
